title: Place_Intent dynamic array (and its cloned type_name strings in load_demo_replay) are never freed
detail: run_demo frees each place's cloned type_name but never delete(demo.places) — the new dynamic array's backing buffer leaks every demo run. load_demo_replay frees neither the places array nor its clones; only clone-loop cleanup exists.
recommended_fix: Add delete(demo.places) to run_demo's defer, and delete(demo.places) plus a type_name-free loop in load_demo_replay (mirroring demo_replay_destroy's node handling).

title: place-verb coordinates silently wrap i64->i32 instead of rejecting out-of-range values
detail: parse_int yields i64; i32(px) truncates bits, so e.g. 4294967296 wraps to tile 0 — an on-map coordinate that passes placement_valid. The parser fails loud on non-numeric input but silently accepts wrap-into-bounds positions.
recommended_fix: Range-check before narrowing: reject px/py outside the i32 range (or outside -map_w_tiles..map_w_tiles) with the same one-line 'bad place position' error, mirroring the fail-loud parse convention.

title: Placement movement guard compares against a stale app.press after tray-chip re-arm
detail: app.press is written only on a placing-press; the chip branch (re)arms placement without resetting it. Releasing a chip click within 6px of a previous placement press point drops a router with no fresh map press — the guard's purpose.
recommended_fix: Reset app.press (e.g. to {-1e9, -1e9}) in the chip branch when arming placement, or require a fresh press flag set only in the placing-press branch before honoring a release.
